doc.title: Billie Pierce and De De Pierce Interview, 1959-04-02

title: Billie tells De De herself on Decatur Street
summary: Billie waits for the trumpeter to pick her up after work and tells him directly that she likes him.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: Now listen, I, alright. Now he was playing music with my sister. Uh-huh, yeah. See? And I was playing in another band, see? Oh, I bet you, yeah. See? Now he was working in one block, like this block, and I was working in the next block, on Decatur Street. So finally, I said, if you don't tell him I like him, I'm going to tell him myself. She said, well, you tell him. I'm sure I'm going to tell him. So my sister used to come and pick me up, you see, when she knocked off before I was, she'd come pick me up. Well, her and sometimes D.D. would come with her, you know, and sit down and play, you know, in my truck and play or play, see? Yeah. And I was having fun. Funny one night, D.D. came in there by herself to pick me up. She told him to come pick me up because she was feeling bad she was going in. Because I had to work about an hour later than she did. So I seen D.D. came in there, you know. D.D. said, Billy, Sadie told me to wait for you because she wasn't feeling too good she was going in. I said, okay. So, oh, that just made me feel good. I was going to walk home that morning. I wasn't going to catch no cab to go home. But D.D. catch a cab ride in, but I was going to walk in that morning. So, all right, so D.D. stayed there, shot knocked off. Band was all coming all together, you know. I think the other boys had to go that direction. Well, I come in my direction. So, maybe he come. We stopped in different places. We get us a little drink, you know. Come on. Get us a little drink. We walked on there. So I told D.D. I said, D.D. He said, huh. I said, listen, I said, did you get a message? He said, a message from who? He got very serious, you know. Yeah. He said, a message from who? I said, say, didn't tell you anything? He said, no, say, didn't tell me anything. He said, what you told Sady something to tell me? I said, yeah. He said, what did you tell Sady? I said, I told Sady to tell you I like the hell out of you. Then he said, shut up. I said, sure, I'm not kidding. Then he said, I been liking you, but I know how to get up that thing. Because every time he see me, I was riding with a bunch of fellas, you know, have my fun, you know. Let's have my fun. You know, what's that to tell us? You know, nothing like that. Then he said, you mean that? I said, shut up. I said, sure. Shut up, child. Yeah. Did he come pick me up every night, bring me home. I said, say, you go ahead home. I said, did he go bring me in. So, D and I, we must run together about three weeks. We decided to get married. So, when I told my sister Sady, I said, I'm going to get married. He said, married who? He said, who in the fool going to tell you crazy to marry something like you? I said, I said, me and Diddy go get married. She said, Billy, no, you ain't. I said, yes, I am too. She said, mm-mm. She said, well, I'm going to tell you one thing. She said, listen. She said, I'm going to tell you. Diddy is a fine fella. Diddy is a real sweet, nice fella. He's from a nice family, Billy. She said, I wouldn't want you to marry Diddy and make his life miserable. If you don't meet Diddy no good, I wouldn't advise you to marry. She said, because I know you. Just like that. She said, no, she didn't think I would ever settle down or anything. Because I was traveling to show and going all the time. I said, well, I made up my mind to settle down. I said, I find a man I love, I'm going to marry him. And from that day, to this day, D and I are still together. That's right. That's right.
